060/**
061 * Bean context.
062 *
063 * <p>
064 * This class servers multiple purposes:
065 * <ul class='spaced-list'>
066 *    <li>
067 *       Provides the ability to wrap beans inside {@link Map} interfaces.
068 *    <li>
069 *       Serves as a repository for metadata on POJOs, such as associated {@link Bean @Marshalled} annotations,
070 *       {@link PropertyNamer PropertyNamers}, etc...  which are used to tailor how POJOs are serialized and parsed.
071 * </ul>
072 *
073 * <p>
074 * All serializers and parsers use this context so that they can handle POJOs using a common framework.
075 *
076 * <h2 class='topic'>Bean Contexts</h2>
077 *
078 * <p>
079 * Bean contexts are created through the {@link MarshallingContext#create() MarshallingContext.create()} and {@link Builder#build()} methods.
080 * <br>These context objects are read-only, reusable, and thread-safe.
081 *
082 * <p>
083 * Each bean context maintains a cache of {@link ClassMeta} objects that describe information about classes encountered.
084 * These <c>ClassMeta</c> objects are time-consuming to construct.
085 * Therefore, instances of {@link MarshallingContext} that share the same <js>"MarshallingContext.*"</js> property values share
086 * the same cache.  This allows for efficient reuse of <c>ClassMeta</c> objects so that the information about
087 * classes only needs to be calculated once.
088 * Because of this, many of the properties defined on the {@link MarshallingContext} class cannot be overridden on the session.
089 *
090 * <h2 class='topic'>Bean Sessions</h2>
091 *
092 * <p>
093 * Whereas <c>MarshallingContext</c> objects are permanent, unchangeable, cached, and thread-safe,
094 * {@link MarshallingSession} objects are ephemeral and not thread-safe.
095 * They are meant to be used as quickly-constructed scratchpads for creating bean maps.
096 * {@link BeanMap} objects can only be created through the session.
097 *
098 * <h2 class='topic'>MarshallingContext configuration properties</h2>
099 *
100 * <p>
101 * <c>BeanContexts</c> have several configuration properties that can be used to tweak behavior on how beans are
102 * handled.  These are denoted as the static <jsf>BEAN_*</jsf> fields on this class.
103 *
104 * <p>
105 * Some settings (e.g. {@link Builder#beansRequireDefaultConstructor()}) are used to differentiate between bean
106 * and non-bean classes.
107 * Attempting to create a bean map around one of these objects will throw a {@link BeanRuntimeException}.
108 * The purpose for this behavior is so that the serializers can identify these non-bean classes and convert them to
109 * plain strings using the {@link Object#toString()} method.
110 *
111 * <p>
112 * Some settings (e.g. {@link Builder#beanFieldVisibility(Visibility)}) are used to determine what kinds of properties are
113 * detected on beans.
114 *
115 * <p>
116 * Some settings (e.g. {@link Builder#beanMapPutReturnsOldValue()}) change the runtime behavior of bean maps.
117 *
118 * <h2 class='section'>Example:</h2>
119 *
120 * <p class='bjava'>
121 *    <jc>// Construct a context from scratch.</jc>
122 *    MarshallingContext <jv>marshallingContext</jv> = MarshallingContext
123 *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()
124 *       .beansRequireDefaultConstructor()
125 *       .notBeanClasses(Foo.<jk>class</jk>)
126 *       .build();
127 * </p>
128 *
129 * <h2 class='topic'>Bean Maps</h2>
130 *
131 * <p>
132 * {@link BeanMap BeanMaps} are wrappers around Java beans that allow properties to be retrieved and
133 * set using the common {@link Map#put(Object,Object)} and {@link Map#get(Object)} methods.
134 *
135 * <p>
136 * Bean maps are created in two ways...
137 * <ol>
138 *    <li>{@link MarshallingSession#toBeanMap(Object) MarshallingSession.toBeanMap()} - Wraps an existing bean inside a {@code Map}
139 *       wrapper.
140 *    <li>{@link MarshallingSession#newBeanMap(Class) MarshallingSession.newBeanMap()} - Create a new bean instance wrapped in a
141 *       {@code Map} wrapper.
142 * </ol>
143 *
144 * <h2 class='section'>Example:</h2>
145 *
146 * <p class='bjava'>
147 *    <jc>// A sample bean class</jc>
148 *    <jk>public class</jk> Person {
149 *       <jk>public</jk> String getName();
150 *       <jk>public void</jk> setName(String <jv>name</jv>);
151 *       <jk>public int</jk> getAge();
152 *       <jk>public void</jk> setAge(<jk>int</jk> <jv>age</jv>);
153 *    }
154 *
155 *    <jc>// Create a new bean session</jc>
156 *    MarshallingSession <jv>session</jv> = MarshallingContext.<jsf>DEFAULT</jsf>.createSession();
157 *
158 *    <jc>// Wrap an existing bean in a new bean map</jc>
159 *    BeanMap&lt;Person&gt; <jv>map1</jv> = <jv>session</jv>.toBeanMap(<jk>new</jk> Person());
160 *    <jv>map1</jv>.put(<js>"name"</js>, <js>"John Smith"</js>);
161 *    <jv>map1</jv>.put(<js>"age"</js>, 45);
162 *
163 *    <jc>// Create a new bean instance wrapped in a new bean map</jc>
164 *    BeanMap&lt;Person&gt; <jv>map2</jv> = <jv>session</jv>.newBeanMap(Person.<jk>class</jk>);
165 *    <jv>map2</jv>.put(<js>"name"</js>, <js>"John Smith"</js>);
166 *    <jv>map2</jv>.put(<js>"age"</js>, 45);
167 *    Person <jv>person</jv> = <jv>map2</jv>.getBean();  <jc>// Get the bean instance that was created.</jc>
168 * </p>
169 *
170 * <h2 class='section'>Notes:</h2><ul>
171 *    <li class='note'>This class is thread safe and reusable.
172 * </ul>
173 *
174 * <h2 class='section'>See Also:</h2><ul>
175 *    <li class='link'><a class="doclink" href="https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/BeanContexts">Bean Contexts</a>
176 * </ul>
177 */
178@SuppressWarnings({
179   "java:S1192", // Duplicated literals (argument/property names) read more clearly inline than as constants
180   "java:S1452", // Wildcard required - ClassMeta<?> for parameter resolution and type variables
181   "java:S1612", // Lambdas used instead of method references for readability in complex chained expressions
182   "java:S3776", // findConversion() registers the whole conversion matrix in one method, and resolveClassMeta(Type, ...) dispatches over every Type shape
183   "java:S6539", // Monster class; MarshallingContext is intentionally the central bean-context configuration hub (also covers Collection.toArray() usage)
184   "rawtypes", // Raw types necessary for generic type handling
185   "unchecked" // Type erasure requires unchecked casts
186})

196      private static int integer(boolean...values) {
197         var n = 0;
198         for (var b : values)

200         return n;

433      /**
434       * Minimum bean class visibility.
435       *
436       * <p>
437       * Classes are not considered beans unless they meet the minimum visibility requirements.
438       * For example, if the visibility is <jsf>PUBLIC</jsf> and the bean class is <jk>protected</jk>, then the class
439       * will not be interpreted as a bean class and be serialized as a string.
440       * Use this setting to reduce the visibility requirement.
441       *
442       * <h4 class='section'>Example:</h4>
443       * <p class='bjava'>
444       *    <jc>// A bean with a protected class and one field.</jc>
445       *    <jk>protected class</jk> MyBean {
446       *       <jk>public</jk> String <jf>foo</jf> = <js>"bar"</js>;
447       *    }
448       *
449       *    <jc>// Create a serializer that's capable of serializing the class.</jc>
450       *    WriterSerializer <jv>serializer</jv> = JsonSerializer
451       *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()
452       *       .beanClassVisibility(<jsf>PROTECTED</jsf>)
453       *       .build();
454       *
455       *    <jc>// Produces:  {"foo","bar"}</jc>
456       *    String <jv>json</jv> = <jv>serializer</jv>.write(<jk>new</jk> MyBean());
457       * </p>
458       *
459       * <h4 class='section'>Notes:</h4><ul>
460       *    <li class='note'>The {@link Bean @Marshalled} annotation can be used on a non-public bean class to override this setting.
461       *    <li class='note'>The {@link BeanIgnore @BeanIgnore} annotation can also be used on a public bean class to ignore it as a bean.
462       * </ul>
463       *
464       * <h4 class='section'>See Also:</h4><ul>
465       *    <li class='ja'>{@link BeanConfig#beanClassVisibility()}
466       * </ul>
467       *
468       * @param value
469       *    The new value for this setting.
470       *    <br>The default is {@link Visibility#PUBLIC}.
471       *    <br>Cannot be <jk>null</jk>.
472       * @return This object.
473       */
474      public Builder beanClassVisibility(Visibility value) {
475         beanClassVisibility = reqnn("value", value);
476         return this;
477      }
478
479      /**
480       * Minimum bean constructor visibility.
481       *
482       * <p>
483       * Only look for constructors with the specified minimum visibility.
484       *
485       * <p>
486       * This setting affects the logic for finding no-arg constructors for bean.  Normally, only <jk>public</jk> no-arg
487       * constructors are used.  Use this setting if you want to reduce the visibility requirement.
488       *
489       * <h4 class='section'>Example:</h4>
490       * <p class='bjava'>
491       *    <jc>// A bean with a protected constructor and one field.</jc>
492       *    <jk>public class</jk> MyBean {
493       *       <jk>public</jk> String <jf>foo</jf>;
494       *
495       *       <jk>protected</jk> MyBean() {}
496       *    }
497       *
498       *    <jc>// Create a parser capable of calling the protected constructor.</jc>
499       *    ReaderParser <jv>parser</jv> = ReaderParser
500       *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()
501       *       .beanConstructorVisibility(<jsf>PROTECTED</jsf>)
502       *       .build();
503       *
504       *    <jc>// Use it.</jc>
505       *    MyBean <jv>myBean</jv> = <jv>parser</jv>.read(<js>"{foo:'bar'}"</js>, MyBean.<jk>class</jk>);
506       * </p>
507       *
508       * <h4 class='section'>Notes:</h4><ul>
509       *    <li class='note'>The {@link BeanCtor @BeanCtor} annotation can also be used to expose a non-public constructor.
510       *    <li class='note'>The {@link BeanIgnore @BeanIgnore} annotation can also be used on a public bean constructor to ignore it.
511       * </ul>
512       *
513       * <h4 class='section'>See Also:</h4><ul>
514       *    <li class='ja'>{@link BeanConfig#beanConstructorVisibility()}
515       * </ul>
516       *
517       * @param value
518       *    The new value for this setting.
519       *    <br>The default is {@link Visibility#PUBLIC}.
520       *    <br>Cannot be <jk>null</jk>.
521       * @return This object.
522       */
523      public Builder beanConstructorVisibility(Visibility value) {
524         beanConstructorVisibility = reqnn("value", value);
525         return this;
526      }

541      /**
542       * Convenience method for {@link #beanDictionary(ClassInfo...)} that accepts {@link Class} objects.
543       *
544       * @param values
545       *    The values to add to this setting.
546       *    <br>Cannot contain <jk>null</jk> values.
547       * @return This object.
548       * @see #beanDictionary(ClassInfo...)
549       */
550      public Builder beanDictionary(Class<?>...values) {
551         reqnns("values", values);
552         return beanDictionary(Stream.of(values).map(x -> info(x)).toArray(ClassInfo[]::new));
553      }

555      /**
556       * Bean dictionary.
557       *
558       * <p>
559       * The list of classes that make up the bean dictionary in this bean context.
560       *
561       * <p>
562       * Values are prepended to the list so that later calls can override classes of earlier calls.
563       *
564       * <p>
565       * A dictionary is a name/class mapping used to find class types during parsing when they cannot be inferred
566       * through reflection.  The names are defined through the {@link Marshalled#typeName() @Marshalled(typeName)} annotation defined
567       * on the bean class.  For example, if a class <c>Foo</c> has a type-name of <js>"myfoo"</js>, then it would end up
568       * serialized as <js>"{_type:'myfoo',...}"</js> in JSON
569       * or <js>"&lt;myfoo&gt;...&lt;/myfoo&gt;"</js> in XML.
570       *
571       * <p>
572       * This setting tells the parsers which classes to look for when resolving <js>"_type"</js> attributes.
573       *
574       * <p>
575       * Values can consist of any of the following types:
576       * <ul>
577       *    <li>Any bean class that specifies a value for {@link Marshalled#typeName() @Marshalled(typeName)}.
578       *    <li>Any subclass of {@link BeanDictionaryList} containing a collection of bean classes with type name annotations.
579       *    <li>Any subclass of {@link BeanDictionaryMap} containing a mapping of type names to classes without type name annotations.
580       *    <li>Any array or collection of the objects above.
581       * </ul>
582       *
583       * <h4 class='section'>Example:</h4>
584       * <p class='bjava'>
585       *    <jc>// POJOs with @Marshalled(name) annotations.</jc>
586       *    <ja>@Marshalled</ja>(typeName=<js>"foo"</js>)
587       *    <jk>public class</jk> Foo {...}
588       *    <ja>@Marshalled</ja>(typeName=<js>"bar"</js>)
589       *    <jk>public class</jk> Bar {...}
590       *
591       *    <jc>// Create a parser and tell it which classes to try to resolve.</jc>
592       *    ReaderParser <jv>parser</jv> = JsonParser
593       *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()
594       *       .dictionary(Foo.<jk>class</jk>, Bar.<jk>class</jk>)
595       *       .addBeanTypes()
596       *       .build();
597       *
598       *    <jc>// A bean with a field with an indeterminate type.</jc>
599       *    <jk>public class</jk> MyBean {
600       *       <jk>public</jk> Object <jf>mySimpleField</jf>;
601       *    }
602       *
603       *    <jc>// Parse bean.</jc>
604       *    MyBean <jv>myBean</jv> = <jv>parser</jv>.read(<js>"{mySimpleField:{_type:'foo',...}}"</js>, MyBean.<jk>class</jk>);
605       * </p>
606       *
607       * <p>
608       * Another option is to use the {@link Marshalled#dictionary()} annotation on the POJO class itself:
609       *
610       * <p class='bjava'>
611       *    <jc>// Instead of by parser, define a bean dictionary on a class through an annotation.</jc>
612       *    <jc>// This applies to all properties on this class and all subclasses.</jc>
613       *    <ja>@Marshalled</ja>(dictionary={Foo.<jk>class</jk>,Bar.<jk>class</jk>})
614       *    <jk>public class</jk> MyBean {
615       *       <jk>public</jk> Object <jf>mySimpleField</jf>;  <jc>// May contain Foo or Bar object.</jc>
616       *       <jk>public</jk> Map&lt;String,Object&gt; <jf>myMapField</jf>;  <jc>// May contain Foo or Bar objects.</jc>
617       *    }
618       * </p>
619       *
620       * <p>
621       *    A typical usage is to allow for HTML documents to be parsed back into HTML beans:
622       * <p class='bjava'>
623       *    <jc>// Use the predefined HTML5 bean dictionary which is a BeanDictionaryList.</jc>
624       *    ReaderParser <jv>parser</jv> = HtmlParser
625       *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()
626       *       .dictionary(HtmlBeanDictionary.<jk>class</jk>)
627       *       .build();
628       *
629       *    <jc>// Parse an HTML body into HTML beans.</jc>
630       *    Body <jv>body</jv> = <jv>parser</jv>.read(<js>"&lt;body&gt;&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;foo&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;bar&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;"</js>, Body.<jk>class</jk>);
631       * </p>
632       *
633       * <h4 class='section'>See Also:</h4><ul>
634       *    <li class='ja'>{@link Marshalled#dictionary()}
635       *    <li class='ja'>{@link MarshalledProp#dictionary()}
636       *    <li class='ja'>{@link MarshalledConfig#dictionary()}
637       *    <li class='ja'>{@link MarshalledConfig#dictionary_replace()}
638       *    <li class='jm'>{@link MarshallingContext.Builder#beanDictionary(ClassInfo...)}
639       * </ul>
640       *
641       * @param values
642       *    The values to add to this setting.
643       *    <br>Cannot contain <jk>null</jk> values.
644       * @return This object.
645       */
646      public Builder beanDictionary(ClassInfo...values) {
647         reqnns("values", values);
648         return beanDictionary(l(values));
649      }
650
651      /**
652       * Same as {@link #beanDictionary(ClassInfo...)} but allows you to pass in a collection of class info objects.
653       *
654       * @param values
655       *    The values to add to this setting.
656       *    <br>Cannot be <jk>null</jk> or contain <jk>null</jk> values.
657       * @return This object.
658       * @see #beanDictionary(ClassInfo...)
659       */
660      public Builder beanDictionary(Collection<ClassInfo> values) {
661         reqnns("values", values);
662         beanDictionary().addAll(0, values);
663         return this;
664      }

666      /**
667       * Minimum bean field visibility.
668       *
669       * <p>
670       * Only look for bean fields with the specified minimum visibility.
671       *
672       * <p>
673       * This affects which fields on a bean class are considered bean properties.  Normally only <jk>public</jk> fields are considered.
674       * Use this setting if you want to reduce the visibility requirement.
675       *
676       * <h4 class='section'>Example:</h4>
677       * <p class='bjava'>
678       *    <jc>// A bean with a protected field.</jc>
679       *    <jk>public class</jk> MyBean {
680       *       <jk>protected</jk> String <jf>foo</jf> = <js>"bar"</js>;
681       *    }
682       *
683       *    <jc>// Create a serializer that recognizes the protected field.</jc>
684       *    WriterSerializer <jv>serializer</jv> = JsonSerializer
685       *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()
686       *       .beanFieldVisibility(<jsf>PROTECTED</jsf>)
687       *       .build();
688       *
689       *    <jc>// Produces:  {"foo":"bar"}</jc>
690       *    String <jv>json</jv> = <jv>serializer</jv>.write(<jk>new</jk> MyBean());
691       * </p>
692       *
693       * <p>
694       * Bean fields can be ignored as properties entirely by setting the value to {@link Visibility#NONE}
695       *
696       * <p class='bjava'>
697       *    <jc>// Disable using fields as properties entirely.</jc>
698       *    WriterSerializer <jv>serializer</jv> = JsonSerializer
699       *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()
700       *       .beanFieldVisibility(<jsf>NONE</jsf>)
701       *       .build();
702       * </p>
703       *
704       * <h4 class='section'>Notes:</h4><ul>
705       *    <li class='note'>The {@link BeanProp @BeanProp} annotation can also be used to expose a non-public field.
706       *    <li class='note'>The {@link BeanIgnore @BeanIgnore} annotation can also be used on a public bean field to ignore it as a bean property.
707       * </ul>
708       *
709       * <h4 class='section'>See Also:</h4><ul>
710       *    <li class='ja'>{@link BeanConfig#beanFieldVisibility()}
711       * </ul>
712       *
713       * @param value
714       *    The new value for this setting.
715       *    <br>The default is {@link Visibility#PUBLIC}.
716       *    <br>Cannot be <jk>null</jk>.
717       * @return This object.
718       */
719      public Builder beanFieldVisibility(Visibility value) {
720         beanFieldVisibility = reqnn("value", value);
721         return this;
722      }

724      /**
725       * Bean interceptor.
726       *
727       * <p>
728       * Bean interceptors can be used to intercept calls to getters and setters and alter their values in transit.
729       *
730       * <h4 class='section'>Example:</h4>
731       * <p class='bjava'>
732       *    <jc>// Interceptor that strips out sensitive information.</jc>
733       *    <jk>public class</jk> AddressInterceptor <jk>extends</jk> BeanInterceptor&lt;Address&gt; {
734       *
735       *       <jk>public</jk> Object readProperty(Address <jv>bean</jv>, String <jv>name</jv>, Object <jv>value</jv>) {
736       *          <jk>if</jk> (<js>"taxInfo"</js>.equals(<jv>name</jv>))
737       *             <jk>return</jk> <js>"redacted"</js>;
738       *          <jk>return</jk> <jv>value</jv>;
739       *       }
740       *
741       *       <jk>public</jk> Object writeProperty(Address <jv>bean</jv>, String <jv>name</jv>, Object <jv>value</jv>) {
742       *          <jk>if</jk> (<js>"taxInfo"</js>.equals(<jv>name</jv>) &amp;&amp; <js>"redacted"</js>.equals(<jv>value</jv>))
743       *             <jk>return</jk> TaxInfoUtils.<jsm>lookup</jsm>(<jv>bean</jv>.getStreet(), <jv>bean</jv>.getCity(), <jv>bean</jv>.getState());
744       *          <jk>return</jk> <jv>value</jv>;
745       *       }
746       *    }
747       *
748       *    <jc>// Our bean class.</jc>
749       *    <jk>public class</jk> Address {
750       *       <jk>public</jk> String getTaxInfo() {...}
751       *       <jk>public void</jk> setTaxInfo(String <jv>value</jv>) {...}
752       *    }
753       *
754       *    <jc>// Register filter on serializer or parser.</jc>
755       *    WriterSerializer <jv>serializer</jv> = JsonSerializer
756       *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()
757       *       .beanInterceptor(Address.<jk>class</jk>, AddressInterceptor.<jk>class</jk>)
758       *       .build();
759       *
760       *    <jc>// Produces:  {"taxInfo":"redacted"}</jc>
761       *    String <jv>json</jv> = <jv>serializer</jv>.write(<jk>new</jk> Address());
762       * </p>
763       *
764       * <h4 class='section'>See Also:</h4><ul>
765       *    <li class='jc'>{@link BeanInterceptor}
766       *    <li class='ja'>{@link Marshalled#interceptor() @Marshalled(interceptor)}
767       * </ul>
768       *
769       * @param on The bean that the filter applies to.
770       *    <br>Cannot be <jk>null</jk>.
771       * @param value
772       *    The new value for this setting.
773       *    <br>Cannot be <jk>null</jk>.
774       * @return This object.
775       */
776      public Builder beanInterceptor(Class<?> on, Class<? extends BeanInterceptor<?>> value) {
777         reqnn("on", on);
778         reqnn("value", value);
779         return annotations(MarshalledApplyAnnotation.create(on).value(MarshalledAnnotation.create().interceptor(value).build()).build());
780      }

782      /**
783       * BeanMap.put() returns old property value.
784       *
785       * <p>
786       * When enabled, then the {@link BeanMap#put(String,Object) BeanMap.put()} method will return old property
787       * values.  Otherwise, it returns <jk>null</jk>.
788       *
789       * <p>
790       * Disabled by default because it introduces a slight performance penalty during serialization.
791       *
792       * <h4 class='section'>Example:</h4>

796       *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()
797       *       .beanMapPutReturnsOldValue()
798       *       .build();
799       *
800       *    BeanMap&lt;MyBean&gt; <jv>myBeanMap</jv> = <jv>context</jv>.createSession().toBeanMap(<jk>new</jk> MyBean());
801       *    <jv>myBeanMap</jv>.put(<js>"foo"</js>, <js>"bar"</js>);
802       *    Object <jv>oldValue</jv> = <jv>myBeanMap</jv>.put(<js>"foo"</js>, <js>"baz"</js>);  <jc>// oldValue == "bar"</jc>
803       * </p>
804       *
805       * <h4 class='section'>See Also:</h4><ul>
806       *    <li class='ja'>{@link BeanConfig#beanMapPutReturnsOldValue()}
807       * </ul>
808       *
809       * @return This object.
810       */
811      public Builder beanMapPutReturnsOldValue() {
812         return beanMapPutReturnsOldValue(true);
813      }

819       * @return This object.
820       */
821      public Builder beanMapPutReturnsOldValue(boolean value) {

826      /**
827       * Minimum bean method visibility.
828       *
829       * <p>
830       * Only look for bean methods with the specified minimum visibility.
831       *
832       * <p>
833       * This affects which methods are detected as getters and setters on a bean class. Normally only <jk>public</jk> getters and setters are considered.
834       * Use this setting if you want to reduce the visibility requirement.
835       *
836       * <h4 class='section'>Example:</h4>
837       * <p class='bjava'>
838       *    <jc>// A bean with a protected getter.</jc>
839       *    <jk>public class</jk> MyBean {
840       *       <jk>public</jk> String getFoo() { <jk>return</jk> <js>"foo"</js>; }
841       *       <jk>protected</jk> String getBar() { <jk>return</jk> <js>"bar"</js>; }

848       *       .build();

852       * </p>
853       *
854       * <h4 class='section'>Notes:</h4><ul>
855       *    <li class='note'>The {@link BeanProp @BeanProp} annotation can also be used to expose a non-public method.
856       *    <li class='note'>The {@link BeanIgnore @BeanIgnore} annotation can also be used on a public bean getter/setter to ignore it as a bean property.
857       * </ul>

861       * </ul>

873      /**
874       * Bean property includes.
875       *
876       * <p>
877       * Specifies the set and order of names of properties associated with the bean class.
878       *
879       * <p>
880       * For example, <c>beanProperties(MyBean.<jk>class</jk>, <js>"foo,bar"</js>)</c> means only serialize the <c>foo</c> and
881       * <c>bar</c> properties on the specified bean.  Likewise, parsing will ignore any bean properties not specified
882       * and either throw an exception or silently ignore them depending on whether {@link #ignoreUnknownBeanProperties()}
883       * has been called.
884       *
885       * <p>
886       * This value is entirely optional if you simply want to expose all the getters and public fields on
887       * a class as bean properties.  However, it's useful if you want certain getters to be ignored or you want the properties to be
888       * serialized in a particular order.  Note that on IBM JREs, the property order is the same as the order in the source code,
889       * whereas on Oracle JREs, the order is entirely random.
890       *
891       * <p>
892       * Setting applies to specified class and all subclasses.
893       *
894       * <h4 class='section'>Example:</h4>
895       * <p class='bjava'>
896       *    <jc>// A bean with 3 properties.</jc>
897       *    <jk>public class</jk> MyBean {
898       *       <jk>public</jk> String
899       *          <jf>foo</jf> = <js>"foo"</js>,
900       *          <jf>bar</jf> = <js>"bar"</js>,
901       *          <jf>baz</jf> = <js>"baz"</js>;
902       *    }
903       *
904       *    <jc>// Create a serializer that includes only the 'foo' and 'bar' properties on the MyBean class.</jc>
905       *    WriterSerializer <jv>serializer</jv> = JsonSerializer
906       *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()
907       *       .beanProperties(MyBean.<jk>class</jk>, <js>"foo,bar"</js>)
908       *       .build();
909       *
910       *    <jc>// Produces:  {"foo":"foo","bar":"bar"}</jc>
911       *    String <jv>json</jv> = <jv>serializer</jv>.write(<jk>new</jk> MyBean());
912       * </p>
913       *
914       * <p>
915       * This method is functionally equivalent to the following code:
916       * <p class='bjava'>
917       *    <jv>builder</jv>.annotations(MarshalledAnnotation.<jsm>create</jsm>(<jv>beanClass</jv>).properties(<jv>properties</jv>).build());
918       * </p>
919       *
920       * <h4 class='section'>See Also:</h4><ul>
921       *    <li class='jma'>{@link BeanType#properties()}/{@link BeanType#p()} - On an annotation on the bean class itself.
922       * </ul>
923       *
924       * @param beanClass The bean class.
925       *    <br>Cannot be <jk>null</jk>.
926       * @param properties Comma-delimited list of property names.
927       *    <br>Cannot be <jk>null</jk>.
928       * @return This object.
929       */
930      public Builder beanProperties(Class<?> beanClass, String properties) {
931         reqnn("beanClass", beanClass);
932         reqnn("properties", properties);
933         return annotations(BeanTypeApplyAnnotation.create(beanClass).value(BeanTypeAnnotation.create().p(properties).build()).build());
934      }

936      /**
937       * Bean property includes.
938       *
939       * <p>
940       * Specifies the set and order of names of properties associated with bean classes.
941       *
942       * <p>
943       * For example, <c>beanProperties(AMap.<jsm>of</jsm>(<js>"MyBean"</js>, <js>"foo,bar"</js>))</c> means only serialize the <c>foo</c> and
944       * <c>bar</c> properties on the specified bean.  Likewise, parsing will ignore any bean properties not specified
945       * and either throw an exception or silently ignore them depending on whether {@link #ignoreUnknownBeanProperties()}
946       * has been called.
947       *
948       * <p>
949       * This value is entirely optional if you simply want to expose all the getters and public fields on
950       * a class as bean properties.  However, it's useful if you want certain getters to be ignored or you want the properties to be
951       * serialized in a particular order.  Note that on IBM JREs, the property order is the same as the order in the source code,
952       * whereas on Oracle JREs, the order is entirely random.
953       *
954       * <p>
955       * Setting applies to specified class and all subclasses.
956       *
957       * <h4 class='section'>Example:</h4>
958       * <p class='bjava'>
959       *    <jc>// A bean with 3 properties.</jc>
960       *    <jk>public class</jk> MyBean {
961       *       <jk>public</jk> String
962       *          <jf>foo</jf> = <js>"foo"</js>,
963       *          <jf>bar</jf> = <js>"bar"</js>,
964       *          <jf>baz</jf> = <js>"baz"</js>;
965       *    }
966       *
967       *    <jc>// Create a serializer that includes only the 'foo' and 'bar' properties on the MyBean class.</jc>
968       *    WriterSerializer <jv>serializer</jv> = JsonSerializer
969       *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()
970       *       .beanProperties(AMap.<jsm>of</jsm>(<js>"MyBean"</js>, <js>"foo,bar"</js>))
971       *       .build();
972       *
973       *    <jc>// Produces:  {"foo":"foo","bar":"bar"}</jc>
974       *    String <jv>json</jv> = <jv>serializer</jv>.write(<jk>new</jk> MyBean());
975       * </p>
976       *
977       * <p>
978       * This method is functionally equivalent to the following code for each entry:
979       * <p class='bjava'>
980       *    <jv>builder</jv>.annotations(MarshalledAnnotation.<jsm>create</jsm>(<jv>key</jv>).properties(<jv>value</jv>.toString()).build());
981       * </p>
982       *
983       * <h4 class='section'>See Also:</h4><ul>
984       *    <li class='jma'>{@link BeanType#properties()} / {@link BeanType#p()}- On an annotation on the bean class itself.
985       * </ul>
986       *
987       * @param values
988       *    The values to add to this builder.
989       *    <br>Keys are bean class names which can be a simple name, fully-qualified name, or <js>"*"</js> for all beans.
990       *    <br>Values are comma-delimited lists of property names.  Non-String objects are first converted to Strings.
991       *    <br>Cannot be <jk>null</jk>.
992       * @return This object.
993       */
994      public Builder beanProperties(Map<String,Object> values) {
995         reqnn("values", values);
996         values.forEach((k, v) -> annotations(BeanTypeApplyAnnotation.create(k).value(BeanTypeAnnotation.create().p(s(v)).build()).build()));
997         return this;
998      }

1000      /**
1001       * Bean property includes.
1002       *
1003       * <p>
1004       * Specifies the set and order of names of properties associated with the bean class.
1005       *
1006       * <p>
1007       * For example, <c>beanProperties(<js>"MyBean"</js>, <js>"foo,bar"</js>)</c> means only serialize the <c>foo</c> and
1008       * <c>bar</c> properties on the specified bean.  Likewise, parsing will ignore any bean properties not specified
1009       * and either throw an exception or silently ignore them depending on whether {@link #ignoreUnknownBeanProperties()}
1010       * has been called.
1011       *
1012       * <p>
1013       * This value is entirely optional if you simply want to expose all the getters and public fields on
1014       * a class as bean properties.  However, it's useful if you want certain getters to be ignored or you want the properties to be
1015       * serialized in a particular order.  Note that on IBM JREs, the property order is the same as the order in the source code,
1016       * whereas on Oracle JREs, the order is entirely random.
1017       *
1018       * <p>
1019       * Setting applies to specified class and all subclasses.
1020       *
1021       * <h4 class='section'>Example:</h4>
1022       * <p class='bjava'>
1023       *    <jc>// A bean with 3 properties.</jc>
1024       *    <jk>public class</jk> MyBean {
1025       *       <jk>public</jk> String
1026       *          <jf>foo</jf> = <js>"foo"</js>,
1027       *          <jf>bar</jf> = <js>"bar"</js>,
1028       *          <jf>baz</jf> = <js>"baz"</js>;
1029       *    }
1030       *
1031       *    <jc>// Create a serializer that includes only the 'foo' and 'bar' properties on the MyBean class.</jc>
1032       *    WriterSerializer <jv>serializer</jv> = JsonSerializer
1033       *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()
1034       *       .beanProperties(<js>"MyBean"</js>, <js>"foo,bar"</js>)
1035       *       .build();
1036       *
1037       *    <jc>// Produces:  {"foo":"foo","bar":"bar"}</jc>
1038       *    String <jv>json</jv> = <jv>serializer</jv>.write(<jk>new</jk> MyBean());
1039       * </p>
1040       *
1041       * <p>
1042       * This method is functionally equivalent to the following code:
1043       * <p class='bjava'>
1044       *    <jv>builder</jv>.annotations(MarshalledAnnotation.<jsm>create</jsm>(<jv>beanClassName</jv>).properties(<jv>properties</jv>).build());
1045       * </p>

1249       *    WriterSerializer <jv>serializer</jv> = JsonSerializer
1250       *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()

1519         return this;
1520      }

1522      /**
1523       * Write-only bean properties.
1524       *
1525       * <p>
1526       * Specifies one or more properties on a bean that are write-only despite having valid setters.
1527       * Parsers will parse such properties as usual, but serializers will silently ignore them.
1528       * Note that this is different from the {@link #beanProperties(Class,String) beanProperties}/{@link #beanPropertiesExcludes(Class,String) beanPropertiesExcludes} settings which include or exclude properties
1529       * for both serializers and parsers.
1530       *
1531       * <h4 class='section'>Example:</h4>
1532       * <p class='bjava'>
1533       *    <jc>// A bean with 3 properties.</jc>
1534       *    <jk>public class</jk> MyBean {
1535       *       <jk>public</jk> String <jf>foo</jf>, <jf>bar</jf>, <jf>baz</jf>;
1536       *    }
1537       *
1538       *    <jc>// Create a serializer with write-only property settings.</jc>
1539       *    WriterSerializer <jv>serializer</jv> = JsonSerializer
1540       *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()
1541       *       .beanPropertiesWriteOnly(<js>"MyBean"</js>, <js>"bar,baz"</js>)
1542       *       .build();
1543       *
1544       *    <jc>// Only foo will be serialized.</jc>
1545       *    String <jv>json</jv> = <jv>serializer</jv>.write(<jk>new</jk> MyBean());
1546       *
1547       *    <jc>// Create a parser with write-only property settings.</jc>
1548       *    ReaderParser <jv>parser</jv> = JsonParser
1549       *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()
1550       *       .beanPropertiesWriteOnly(<js>"MyBean"</js>, <js>"bar,baz"</js>)
1551       *       .build();
1552       *
1553       *    <jc>// Parser parses all 3 properties.</jc>
1554       *    MyBean <jv>myBean</jv> = <jv>parser</jv>.read(<js>"{foo:'foo',bar:'bar',baz:'baz'}"</js>, MyBean.<jk>class</jk>);
1555       * </p>
1556       *
1557       * <p>
1558       * This method is functionally equivalent to the following code:
1559       * <p class='bjava'>
1560       *    <jv>builder</jv>.annotations(MarshalledAnnotation.<jsm>create</jsm>(<jv>beanClassName</jv>).writeOnlyProperties(<jv>properties</jv>).build());
1561       * </p>
1562       *
1563       * <h4 class='section'>See Also:</h4><ul>
1564       *    <li class='jma'>{@link BeanType#writeOnlyProperties()} / {@link BeanType#wo()}
1565       * </ul>
1566       *
1567       * @param beanClassName
1568       *    The bean class name.
1569       *    <br>Can be a simple name, fully-qualified name, or <js>"*"</js> for all bean classes.
1570       * @param properties Comma-delimited list of property names.
1571       * @return This object.
1572       */
1573      public Builder beanPropertiesWriteOnly(String beanClassName, String properties) {
1574         reqnn("beanClassName", beanClassName);
1575         reqnn("properties", properties);
1576         return annotations(BeanTypeApplyAnnotation.create(beanClassName).value(BeanTypeAnnotation.create().wo(properties).build()).build());
1577      }

1579      /**
1580       * Beans require no-arg constructors.
1581       *
1582       * <p>
1583       * When enabled, a Java class must implement a default no-arg constructor to be considered a bean.
1584       * Otherwise, the bean will be serialized as a string using the {@link Object#toString()} method.
1585       *
1586       * <h4 class='section'>Example:</h4>
1587       * <p class='bjava'>
1588       *    <jc>// A bean without a no-arg constructor.</jc>
1589       *    <jk>public class</jk> MyBean {
1590       *
1591       *       <jc>// A property method.</jc>
1592       *       <jk>public</jk> String <jf>foo</jf> = <js>"bar"</js>;
1593       *
1594       *       <jc>// A no-arg constructor</jc>
1595       *       <jk>public</jk> MyBean(String <jv>foo</jv>) {
1596       *          <jk>this</jk>.<jf>foo</jf> = <jv>foo</jv>;
1597       *       }
1598       *
1599       *       <ja>@Override</ja>
1600       *       <jk>public</jk> String toString() {
1601       *          <jk>return</jk> <js>"bar"</js>;
1602       *       }
1603       *    }
1604       *
1605       *    <jc>// Create a serializer that ignores beans without default constructors.</jc>
1606       *    WriterSerializer <jv>serializer</jv> = JsonSerializer
1607       *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()
1608       *       .beansRequireDefaultConstructor()
1609       *       .build();
1610       *
1611       *    <jc>// Produces:  "bar"</jc>
1612       *    String <jv>json</jv> = <jv>serializer</jv>.write(<jk>new</jk> MyBean());
1613       * </p>
1614       *
1615       * <h4 class='section'>Notes:</h4><ul>
1616       *    <li class='note'>The {@link Bean @Marshalled} annotation can be used on a bean class to override this setting.
1617       *    <li class='note'>The {@link BeanIgnore @BeanIgnore} annotation can also be used on a class to ignore it as a bean.
1618       * </ul>
1619       *
1620       * <h4 class='section'>See Also:</h4><ul>
1621       *    <li class='ja'>{@link BeanConfig#beansRequireDefaultConstructor()}
1622       * </ul>
1623       *
1624       * @return This object.
1625       */
1626      public Builder beansRequireDefaultConstructor() {
1627         return beansRequireDefaultConstructor(true);
1628      }

1630      /**
1631       * Same as {@link #beansRequireDefaultConstructor()} but allows you to explicitly specify the value.
1632       *
1633       * @param value The value for this setting.
1634       * @return This object.
1635       */
1636      public Builder beansRequireDefaultConstructor(boolean value) {
1637         beansRequireDefaultConstructor = value;
1638         return this;
1639      }

1698      /**
1699       * Beans require setters for getters.
1700       *
1701       * <p>

1704       * <h4 class='section'>Example:</h4>

1706       *    <jc>// A bean without a Serializable interface.</jc>

1713       *       <jc>// A read-only property.</jc>
1714       *       <jk>public</jk> String getBar() { <jk>return</jk> <js>"bar"</js>; }

1749      /**
1750       * Sets the bean store used for factory-based instantiation.
1751       *
1752       * <p>
1753       * The bean store is used to resolve {@link BeanFactory} instances registered via
1754       * <ja>@BeanType</ja><c>(factory=X.class)</c> and <ja>@BeanProp</ja><c>(factory=X.class)</c> annotations.
1755       * When a factory class is encountered, the framework first looks it up in the bean store
1756       * before attempting direct instantiation.
1757       *
1758       * <p>
1759       * Typically set to a {@code SpringBeanStore} wrapping the application's
1760       * {@code ApplicationContext} so that Spring-managed factories are resolved automatically.
1761       *
1762       * <h4 class='section'>Example:</h4>
1763       * <p class='bjava'>
1764       *    <jk>public class</jk> MyRestServlet <jk>extends</jk> BasicRestServlet {
1765       *       <ja>@Autowired</ja> ApplicationContext <jv>ctx</jv>;
1766       *
1767       *       <ja>@Override</ja>
1768       *       <jk>protected</jk> MarshallingContext createBeanContext(MarshallingContext.Builder&lt;?&gt; <jv>builder</jv>) {
1769       *          <jk>return</jk> <jv>builder</jv>.beanStore(<jk>new</jk> SpringBeanStore(<jv>ctx</jv>)).build();
1770       *       }
1771       *    }
1772       * </p>
1773       *
1774       * @param value The bean store, or <jk>null</jk> to use direct instantiation only.
1775       * @return This object.
1776       */
1777      public Builder beanStore(BeanStore value) {
1778         beanStore = value;
1779         return this;
1780      }

1794       *
1795    * @param value The value to copy.  Can be <jk>null</jk> (returns <jk>null</jk>).
1796    * @return A copy of the value, or <jk>null</jk> if the value was <jk>null</jk>.
1797       */
1798      public static Builder copyOrNull(Builder value) {
1799         return value == null ? null : value.copy();

1802      /**
1803       * Bean dictionary.
1804       *
1805       * <p>
1806       * This is identical to {@link #beanDictionary(Class...)}, but specifies a dictionary within the context of
1807       * a single class as opposed to globally.
1808       *
1809       * <h4 class='section'>Example:</h4>
1810       * <p class='bjava'>
1811       *    <jc>// POJOs with @Marshalled(name) annotations.</jc>
1812       *    <ja>@Marshalled</ja>(typeName=<js>"foo"</js>)
1813       *    <jk>public class</jk> Foo {...}
1814       *    <ja>@Marshalled</ja>(typeName=<js>"bar"</js>)
1815       *    <jk>public class</jk> Bar {...}
1816       *
1817       *    <jc>// A bean with a field with an indeterminate type.</jc>
1818       *    <jk>public class</jk> MyBean {
1819       *       <jk>public</jk> Object <jf>mySimpleField</jf>;
1820       *    }
1821       *
1822       *    <jc>// Create a parser and tell it which classes to try to resolve.</jc>
1823       *    ReaderParser <jv>parser</jv> = JsonParser
1824       *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()
1825       *       .dictionaryOn(MyBean.<jk>class</jk>, Foo.<jk>class</jk>, Bar.<jk>class</jk>)
1826       *       .build();
1827       *
1828       *    <jc>// Parse bean.</jc>
1829       *    MyBean <jv>myBean</jv> = <jv>parser</jv>.read(<js>"{mySimpleField:{_type:'foo',...}}"</js>, MyBean.<jk>class</jk>);
1830       * </p>
1831       *
1832       * <p>
1833       * This is functionally equivalent to the {@link Marshalled#dictionary()} annotation.
1834       *
1835       * <h4 class='section'>See Also:</h4><ul>
1836       *    <li class='jma'>{@link Marshalled#dictionary()}
1837       *    <li class='jm'>{@link #beanDictionary(Class...)}
1838       * </ul>
1839       *
1840       * @param on The class that the dictionary values apply to.
1841       * @param values
1842       *    The new values for this setting.
1843       * @return This object.
1844       */
1845      public Builder dictionaryOn(Class<?> on, Class<?>...values) {
1846         reqnn("on", on);
1847         reqnns("values", values);
1848         return annotations(MarshalledApplyAnnotation.create(on).value(MarshalledAnnotation.create().dictionary(values).build()).build());
1849      }

1871       *       .build();

1904       * Don't silently ignore missing setters.
1905       *
1906       * <p>
1907       * When enabled, trying to set a value on a bean property without a setter will throw a {@link BeanRuntimeException}.

1927       * </p>

2081       *
2082       * <p>
2083       * Examples are used in cases such as POJO examples in Swagger documents.
2084       *
2085       * <p>
2086       * Setting applies to specified class and all subclasses.
2087       *
2088       * <h4 class='section'>Example:</h4>
2089       * <p class='bjava'>
2090       *    <jc>// Create a serializer that excludes the 'foo' and 'bar' properties on the MyBean class.</jc>
2091       *    WriterSerializer <jv>serializer</jv> = JsonSerializer
2092       *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()
2093       *       .example(MyBean.<jk>class</jk>, <js>"{foo:'bar'}"</js>)
2094       *       .build();
2095       * </p>
2096       *
2097       * <p>
2098       * This is a shorthand method for the following code:
2099       * <p class='bjava'>
2100       *    <jv>builder</jv>.annotations(MarshalledAnnotation.<jsm>create</jsm>(<jv>pojoClass</jv>).example(<jv>json</jv>).build())
2101       * </p>
2102       *
2103       * <p>
2104       * POJO examples can also be defined on classes via the following:
2105       * <ul class='spaced-list'>
2106       *    <li>A static field annotated with {@link Example @Example}.
2107       *    <li>A static method annotated with {@link Example @Example} with zero arguments or one {@link MarshallingSession} argument.
2108       *    <li>A static method with name <c>example</c> with no arguments or one {@link MarshallingSession} argument.
2109       * </ul>
2110       *
2111       * <h4 class='section'>See Also:</h4><ul>
2112       *    <li class='ja'>{@link Marshalled#example()}
2113       * </ul>
2114       *
2115       * @param <T> The POJO class type.
2116       * @param pojoClass The POJO class.
2117       *    <br>Cannot be <jk>null</jk>.
2118       * @param json The JSON 5 representation of the example.
2119       *    <br>Can be <jk>null</jk> or empty (treated as no example).
2120       * @return This object.
2121       */
2122      public <T> Builder example(Class<T> pojoClass, String json) {
2123         return annotations(MarshalledApplyAnnotation.create(reqnn("pojoClass", pojoClass)).value(MarshalledAnnotation.create().example(json).build()).build());
2124      }

2126      /**
2127       * POJO example.
2128       *
2129       * <p>
2130       * Specifies an example of the specified class.
2131       *
2132       * <p>
2133       * Examples are used in cases such as POJO examples in Swagger documents.
2134       *
2135       * <h4 class='section'>Example:</h4>
2136       * <p class='bjava'>
2137       *    <jc>// Create a serializer that excludes the 'foo' and 'bar' properties on the MyBean class.</jc>
2138       *    WriterSerializer <jv>serializer</jv> = JsonSerializer
2139       *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()
2140       *       .example(MyBean.<jk>class</jk>, <jk>new</jk> MyBean().setFoo(<js>"foo"</js>).setBar(123))
2141       *       .build();
2142       * </p>
2143       *
2144       * <p>
2145       * This is a shorthand method for the following code:
2146       * <p class='bjava'>
2147       *       <jv>builder</jv>.annotations(MarshalledAnnotation.<jsm>create</jsm>(<jv>pojoClass</jv>).example(Json5.<jsf>DEFAULT</jsf>.toString(<jv>object</jv>)).build())
2148       * </p>
2149       *
2150       * <h4 class='section'>Notes:</h4><ul>
2151       *    <li class='note'>Using this method assumes the serialized form of the object is the same as that produced
2152       *       by the default serializer.  This may not be true based on settings or swaps on the constructed serializer.
2153       * </ul>
2154       *
2155       * <p>
2156       * POJO examples can also be defined on classes via the following:
2157       * <ul class='spaced-list'>
2158       *    <li>The {@link Marshalled#example()} annotation on the class itself.
2159       *    <li>A static field annotated with {@link Example @Example}.
2160       *    <li>A static method annotated with {@link Example @Example} with zero arguments or one {@link MarshallingSession} argument.
2161       *    <li>A static method with name <c>example</c> with no arguments or one {@link MarshallingSession} argument.
2162       * </ul>
2163       *
2164       * @param <T> The POJO class.
2165       * @param pojoClass The POJO class.
2166       *    <br>Cannot be <jk>null</jk>.
2167       * @param o
2168       *    An instance of the POJO class used for examples.
2169       *    <br>Can be <jk>null</jk> (will be serialized as <js>"null"</js>).
2170       * @return This object.
2171       */
2172      public <T> Builder example(Class<T> pojoClass, T o) {
2173         return annotations(MarshalledApplyAnnotation.create(reqnn("pojoClass", pojoClass)).value(MarshalledAnnotation.create().example(Json5.of(o)).build()).build());
2174      }

2176      /**
2177       * Find fluent setters.
2178       *
2179       * <p>
2180       * When enabled, fluent setters are detected on beans during parsing.
2181       *
2182       * <p>
2183       * Fluent setters must have the following attributes:
2184       * <ul>
2185       *    <li>Public.
2186       *    <li>Not static.
2187       *    <li>Take in one parameter.
2188       *    <li>Return the bean itself.
2189       * </ul>
2190       *
2191       * <h4 class='section'>Example:</h4>
2192       * <p class='bjava'>
2193       *    <jc>// A bean with a fluent setter.</jc>
2194       *    <jk>public class</jk> MyBean {
2195       *       <jk>public</jk> MyBean foo(String <jv>value</jv>) {...}
2196       *    }
2197       *
2198       *    <jc>// Create a parser that finds fluent setters.</jc>
2199       *    ReaderParser <jv>parser</jv> = JsonParser
2200       *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()
2201       *       .findFluentSetters()
2202       *       .build();
2203       *
2204       *    <jc>// Parse into bean using fluent setter.</jc>
2205       *    MyBean <jv>myBean</jv> = <jv>parser</jv>.read(<js>"{foo:'bar'}"</js>);
2206       * </p>
2207       *
2208       * <h4 class='section'>Notes:</h4><ul>
2209       *    <li class='note'>The {@link BeanProp @BeanProp} annotation can also be used on methods to individually identify them as fluent setters.
2210       *    <li class='note'>The {@link BeanType#findFluentSetters() @BeanType.findFluentSetters()} annotation can also be used on classes to specify to look for fluent setters.
2211       * </ul>
2212       *
2213       * <h4 class='section'>See Also:</h4><ul>
2214       *    <li class='ja'>{@link BeanType#findFluentSetters()}
2215       *    <li class='ja'>{@link BeanConfig#findFluentSetters()}
2216       * </ul>
2217       *
2218       * @return This object.
2219       */
2220      public Builder findFluentSetters() {
2221         return findFluentSetters(true);
2222      }

2224      /**
2225       * Same as {@link #findFluentSetters()} but allows you to explicitly specify the value.

2228       * @return This object.
2229       */
2230      public Builder findFluentSetters(boolean value) {
2231         findFluentSetters = value;
2232         return this;
2233      }

2235      /**
2236       * Find fluent setters.
2237       *
2238       * <p>
2239       * Identical to {@link #findFluentSetters()} but enables it on a specific class only.
2240       *
2241       * <h4 class='section'>Example:</h4>

2246       *    }
2247       *
2248       *    <jc>// Create a parser that finds fluent setters.</jc>

2250       *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()
2251       *       .findFluentSetters(MyBean.<jk>class</jk>)
2252       *       .build();
2253       *
2254       *    <jc>// Parse into bean using fluent setter.</jc>
2255       *    MyBean <jv>myBean</jv> = <jv>parser</jv>.read(<js>"{foo:'bar'}"</js>);
2256       * </p>
2257       *
2258       * <h4 class='section'>Notes:</h4><ul>
2259       *    <li class='note'>This method is functionally equivalent to using the {@link BeanType#findFluentSetters()} annotation.
2260       * </ul>
2261       *
2262       * <h4 class='section'>See Also:</h4><ul>
2263       *    <li class='ja'>{@link BeanType#findFluentSetters()}
2264       *    <li class='jm'>{@link #findFluentSetters()}

2268       *    <br>Cannot be <jk>null</jk>.
2269       * @return This object.

2271      public Builder findFluentSetters(Class<?> on) {
2272         reqnn("on", on);

2339      /**
2340       * Sets the default active view name for all sessions created from this context.
2341       *
2342       * <p>
2343       * When set, only bean properties whose declared {@link MarshalledProp#view()} set contains this view name
2344       * will be included during serialization.  On the parse side, properties outside the active view are routed
2345       * through the existing unknown/ignored-property mechanism governed by
2346       * {@link #ignoreUnknownBeanProperties()}.
2347       *
2348       * <p>
2349       * Untagged properties (those whose declared view set is empty) follow the default-view-inclusion policy:
2350       * included under every active view unless {@link #disableDefaultViewInclusion()} has been called.
2351       *
2352       * <p>
2353       * This value can be overridden per serialization or parse call via the session builder (e.g.
2354       * {@link MarshallingSession.Builder#activeView(String)}).
2355       *
2356       * <h4 class='section'>Example:</h4>
2357       * <p class='bjava'>
2358       *    JsonSerializer <jv>serializer</jv> = JsonSerializer.<jsm>create</jsm>()
2359       *       .activeView(<js>"summary"</js>)
2360       *       .build();
2361       * </p>
2362       *
2363       * <h4 class='section'>See Also:</h4><ul>
2364       *    <li class='ja'>{@link MarshalledProp#view()}
2365       *    <li class='jm'>{@link MarshallingSession.Builder#activeView(String)}
2366       * </ul>
2367       *
2368       * @param value The active view name.  Use <jk>null</jk> to disable view filtering.
2369       * @return This object.
2370       * @since 10.0.0
2371       */
2372      public Builder activeView(String value) {
2373         activeView = value;
2374         return this;
2375      }

2430       *       .build();

2549      /**
2550       * Schema validation mode.
2551       *
2552       * <p>
2553       * When enabled, bean property values are validated against the constraints declared by
2554       * {@link Schema @Schema} annotations on those properties.  Validation runs
2555       * during both <b>parsing</b> (value set on the bean) and <b>serialization</b> (value read from the bean).
2556       *
2557       * <p>
2558       * Backed by the typed {@code JsonSchema} bean in {@code juneau-bean-jsonschema} and JSON Schema Draft 2020-12
2559       * semantics.  Validation failures throw {@link SchemaValidationException}
2560       * wrapped in {@code BeanRuntimeException}; the parser surfaces them as
2561       * {@link ParseException} and the serializer surfaces them as
2562       * {@link SerializeException}.
2563       *
2564       * <p>
2565       * If {@code juneau-bean-jsonschema} is not on the classpath, this flag becomes a silent no-op.
2566       *
2567       * <h4 class='section'>Example:</h4>
2568       * <p class='bjava'>
2569       *    <jc>// A bean with a length-constrained property.</jc>
2570       *    <jk>public class</jk> MyBean {
2571       *       <ja>&#64;Schema</ja>(minLength=<js>"2"</js>, maxLength=<js>"10"</js>)
2572       *       <jk>public</jk> String <jf>name</jf>;
2573       *    }
2574       *
2575       *    <jc>// Parser that validates inbound values.</jc>
2576       *    ReaderParser <jv>p</jv> = JsonParser.<jsm>create</jsm>().validateSchema().build();
2577       *
2578       *    <jv>p</jv>.read(<js>"{name:'a'}"</js>, MyBean.<jk>class</jk>);  <jc>// throws ParseException - too short</jc>
2579       * </p>
2580       *
2581       * <h4 class='section'>See Also:</h4><ul>
2582       *    <li class='ja'>{@link BeanConfig#validateSchema()}
2583       * </ul>
2584       *
2585       * @return This object.
2586       * @since 10.0.0
2587       */
2588      public Builder validateSchema() {
2589         return validateSchema(true);
2590      }

2598       */

2631      /**
2632       * Implementation classes.
2633       *
2634       * <p>
2635       * For interfaces and abstract classes this method can be used to specify an implementation class for the
2636       * interface/abstract class so that instances of the implementation class are used when instantiated (e.g. during a
2637       * parse).
2638       *
2639       * <h4 class='section'>Example:</h4>
2640       * <p class='bjava'>
2641       *    <jc>// A bean interface.</jc>
2642       *    <jk>public interface</jk> MyBean {
2643       *       ...
2644       *    }
2645       *
2646       *    <jc>// A bean implementation.</jc>
2647       *    <jk>public class</jk> MyBeanImpl <jk>implements</jk> MyBean {
2648       *       ...
2649       *    }
2650
2651       *    <jc>// Create a parser that instantiates MyBeanImpls when parsing MyBeans.</jc>
2652       *    ReaderParser <jv>parser</jv> = JsonParser
2653       *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()
2654       *       .implClass(MyBean.<jk>class</jk>, MyBeanImpl.<jk>class</jk>)
2655       *       .build();
2656       *
2657       *    <jc>// Instantiates a MyBeanImpl,</jc>
2658       *    MyBean <jv>myBean</jv> = <jv>parser</jv>.read(<js>"..."</js>, MyBean.<jk>class</jk>);
2659       * </p>
2660       *
2661       * @param interfaceClass The interface class.
2662       *    <br>Cannot be <jk>null</jk>.
2663       * @param implClass The implementation class.
2664       *    <br>Cannot be <jk>null</jk>.

3172       *    String <jv>json</jv> = <jv>serializer</jv>.write(<jk>new</jk> MyBean());

3176       *    <li class='note'>The {@link BeanType#unsorted() @BeanType.unsorted()} annotation can also be used to opt out of sorting on a single class.

3199       * <p>
3200       * By default, record properties are sorted alphabetically like every other bean.  Calling this method makes
3201       * records keep their component (declaration) order, even when other beans are sorted.  Non-record beans are
3202       * unaffected.
3203       *
3204       * <h4 class='section'>Example:</h4>
3205       * <p class='bjava'>
3206       *    <jk>public record</jk> Person(String <jv>name</jv>, <jk>int</jk> <jv>age</jv>) {}
3207       *
3208       *    WriterSerializer <jv>serializer</jv> = JsonSerializer
3209       *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()
3210       *       .recordComponentOrder()
3211       *       .build();
3212       *
3213       *    <jc>// Produces:  {"name":"Alice","age":30}</jc>
3214       *    String <jv>json</jv> = <jv>serializer</jv>.write(<jk>new</jk> Person(<js>"Alice"</js>, 30));
3215       * </p>
3216       *
3217       * <h4 class='section'>See Also:</h4><ul>
3218       *    <li class='jm'>{@link #unsortedProperties()} (declaration order for every bean, records included)
3219       *    <li class='ja'>{@link BeanConfig#recordComponentOrder()}
3220       * </ul>
3221       *
3222       * @return This object.
3223       */
3224      public Builder recordComponentOrder() {
3225         return recordComponentOrder(true);
3226      }

3232       * @return This object.
3233       */
3234      public Builder recordComponentOrder(boolean value) {
3235         recordComponentOrder = value;
3236         return this;
3237      }

3239      /**
3240       * Opt specific bean classes out of alphabetical property sorting.

3242       * <p>
3243       * Applies the {@link BeanType#unsorted() @BeanType(unsorted=true)} annotation to the specified classes,
3244       * overriding the default sorted behavior for those specific beans.

3247       *    <li class='ja'>{@link BeanType#unsorted() @BeanType(unsorted)}
3248       * </ul>

3250       * @param on The bean classes to opt out of sorted properties.
3251       *    <br>Cannot contain <jk>null</jk> values.
3252       * @return This object.

3254      public Builder unsortedProperties(Class<?>...on) {
3255         reqnns("on", on);

3261      /**
3262       * Identifies a stop class for the annotated class.
3263       *
3264       * <p>
3265       * Identical in purpose to the stop class specified by {@link Introspector#getBeanInfo(Class, Class)}.
3266       * Any properties in the stop class or in its base classes will be ignored during analysis.
3267       *
3268       * <p>
3269       * For example, in the following class hierarchy, instances of <c>C3</c> will include property <c>p3</c>,
3270       * but not <c>p1</c> or <c>p2</c>.
3271       *
3272       * <h4 class='section'>Example:</h4>
3273       * <p class='bjava'>
3274       *    <jk>public class</jk> C1 {
3275       *       <jk>public int</jk> getP1();
3276       *    }
3277       *
3278       *    <jk>public class</jk> C2 <jk>extends</jk> C1 {
3279       *       <jk>public int</jk> getP2();
3280       *    }
3281       *
3282       *    <jk>public class</jk> C3 <jk>extends</jk> C2 {
3283       *       <jk>public int</jk> getP3();
3284       *    }
3285       *
3286       *    <jc>// Create a serializer specifies a stop class for C3.</jc>
3287       *    WriterSerializer <jv>serializer</jv> = JsonSerializer
3288       *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()
3289       *       .stopClass(C3.<jk>class</jk>, C2.<jk>class</jk>)
3290       *       .build();
3291       *
3292       *    <jc>// Produces:  {"p3":"..."}</jc>
3293       *    String <jv>json</jv> = <jv>serializer</jv>.write(<jk>new</jk> C3());
3294       * </p>
3295       *
3296       * @param on The class on which the stop class is being applied.
3297       *    <br>Cannot be <jk>null</jk>.
3298       * @param value
3299       *    The new value for this setting.
3300       *    <br>Cannot be <jk>null</jk>.
3301       * @return This object.
3302       */
3303      public Builder stopClass(Class<?> on, Class<?> value) {
3304         reqnn("on", on);
3305         reqnn("value", value);
3306         return annotations(BeanTypeApplyAnnotation.create(on).value(BeanTypeAnnotation.create().stopClass(value).build()).build());
3307      }

3309      /**
3310       * A shortcut for defining a {@link FunctionalSwap}.
3311       *
3312       * <h4 class='section'>Example:</h4>
3313       * <p class='bjava'>
3314       *    <jc>// Create a serializer that performs a custom format for DAte objects.</jc>
3315       *    WriterSerializer <jv>serializer</jv> = JsonSerializer
3316       *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()
3317       *       .swap(Date.<jk>class</jk>, String.<jk>class</jk>, <jv>x</jv> -&gt; <jsm>format</jsm>(<jv>x</jv>))
3318       *       .build();
3319       * </p>
3320       *
3321       * @param <T> The object type being swapped out.
3322       * @param <S> The object type being swapped in.
3323       * @param normalClass The object type being swapped out.
3324       *    <br>Cannot be <jk>null</jk>.
3325       * @param swappedClass The object type being swapped in.
3326       *    <br>Cannot be <jk>null</jk>.
3327       * @param swapFunction The function to convert the object.
3328       *    <br>Cannot be <jk>null</jk>.
3329       * @return This object.
3330       */
3331      public <T,S> Builder swap(Class<T> normalClass, Class<S> swappedClass, ThrowingFunction<T,S> swapFunction) {
3332         reqnn("normalClass", normalClass);
3333         reqnn("swappedClass", swappedClass);
3334         reqnn("swapFunction", swapFunction);
3335         swaps().add(0, new FunctionalSwap<>(normalClass, swappedClass, swapFunction, null));
3336         return this;
3337      }

3339      /**

3357       * @param swapFunction The function to convert the object during serialization.
3358       *    <br>Cannot be <jk>null</jk>.
3359       * @param unswapFunction The function to convert the object during parsing.
3360       *    <br>Cannot be <jk>null</jk>.
3361       * @return This object.
3362       */
3363      public <T,S> Builder swap(Class<T> normalClass, Class<S> swappedClass, ThrowingFunction<T,S> swapFunction, ThrowingFunction<S,T> unswapFunction) {

3404      /**
3405       * Java object swaps.
3406       *
3407       * <p>
3408       * Swaps are used to "swap out" non-serializable classes with serializable equivalents during serialization,
3409       * and "swap in" the non-serializable class during parsing.
3410       *
3411       * <p>
3412       * An example of a swap would be a <c>Calendar</c> object that gets swapped out for an ISO8601 string.
3413       *
3414       * <p>
3415       * Multiple swaps can be associated with a single class.
3416       * When multiple swaps are applicable to the same class, the media type pattern defined by
3417       * {@link ObjectSwap#forMediaTypes()} or {@link Swap#mediaTypes() @Swap(mediaTypes)} are used to come up with the best match.
3418       *
3419       * <p>
3420       * Values can consist of any of the following types:
3421       * <ul>
3422       *    <li>Any subclass of {@link ObjectSwap}.
3423       *    <li>Any instance of {@link ObjectSwap}.
3424       *    <li>Any surrogate class.  A shortcut for defining a {@link SurrogateSwap}.
3425       *    <li>Any array or collection of the objects above.
3426       * </ul>
3427       *
3428       * <h4 class='section'>Example:</h4>
3429       * <p class='bjava'>
3430       *    <jc>// Sample swap for converting Dates to ISO8601 strings.</jc>
3431       *    <jk>public class</jk> MyDateSwap <jk>extends</jk> StringSwap&lt;Date&gt; {
3432       *       <jc>// ISO8601 formatter.</jc>
3433       *       <jk>private</jk> DateFormat <jf>format</jf> = <jk>new</jk> SimpleDateFormat(<js>"yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ssZ"</js>);
3434       *
3435       *       <ja>@Override</ja>
3436       *       <jk>public</jk> String swap(MarshallingSession <jv>session</jv>, Date <jv>date</jv>) {
3437       *          <jk>return</jk> <jf>format</jf>.format(<jv>date</jv>);
3438       *       }
3439       *
3440       *       <ja>@Override</ja>
3441       *       <jk>public</jk> Date unswap(MarshallingSession <jv>session</jv>, String <jv>string</jv>, ClassMeta <jv>hint</jv>) <jk>throws</jk> Exception {
3442       *          <jk>return</jk> <jf>format</jf>.parse(<jv>string</jv>);
3443       *       }
3444       *    }
3445       *
3446       *    <jc>// Sample bean with a Date field.</jc>
3447       *    <jk>public class</jk> MyBean {
3448       *       <jk>public</jk> Date <jf>date</jf> = <jk>new</jk> Date(112, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6);
3449       *    }
3450       *
3451       *    <jc>// Create a serializer that uses our date swap.</jc>
3452       *    WriterSerializer <jv>serializer</jv> = JsonSerializer
3453       *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()
3454       *       .swaps(MyDateSwap.<jk>class</jk>)
3455       *       .build();
3456       *
3457       *    <jc>// Produces:  {"date":"2012-03-03T04:05:06-0500"}</jc>
3458       *    String <jv>json</jv> = <jv>serializer</jv>.write(<jk>new</jk> MyBean());
3459       *
3460       *    <jc>// Create a serializer that uses our date swap.</jc>
3461       *    ReaderParser <jv>parser</jv> = JsonParser
3462       *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()
3463       *       .swaps(MyDateSwap.<jk>class</jk>)
3464       *       .build();
3465       *
3466       *    <jc>// Use our parser to parse a bean.</jc>
3467       *    MyBean <jv>bean</jv> = <jv>parser</jv>.read(<jv>json</jv>, MyBean.<jk>class</jk>);
3468       * </p>
3469       *
3470       * <h4 class='section'>Notes:</h4><ul>
3471       *    <li class='note'>The {@link Swap @Swap} annotation can also be used on classes to identify swaps for the class.
3472       *    <li class='note'>The {@link Swap @Swap} annotation can also be used on bean methods and fields to identify swaps for values of those bean properties.
3473       * </ul>
3474       *
3475       * @param values
3476       *    The values to add to this setting.
3477       *    <br>Values can consist of any of the following types:
3478       *    <ul>
3479       *       <li>Any subclass of {@link ObjectSwap}.
3480       *       <li>Any surrogate class.  A shortcut for defining a {@link SurrogateSwap}.
3481       *       <li>Any array/collection/stream of the objects above.
3482       *    </ul>
3483       *    <br>Cannot be <jk>null</jk>.
3484       * @return This object.
3485       */
3486      public Builder swaps(Object...values) {
3487         reqnns("values", values);
3488         swaps().addAll(0, accumulate(values));
3489         return this;
3490      }

3492      /**
3493       * <i><l>Context</l> configuration property:&emsp;</i>  TimeZone.
3494       *
3495       * <p>
3496       * Specifies the default time zone for serializer and parser sessions when not specified via {@link MarshallingSession.Builder#timeZone(TimeZone)}.
3497       * Typically used for POJO swaps that need to deal with timezones such as swaps that convert <l>Date</l> and <l>Calendar</l>
3498       * objects to strings by accessing it via the session passed into the {@link ObjectSwap#swap(MarshallingSession, Object)} and
3499       * {@link ObjectSwap#unswap(MarshallingSession, Object, ClassMeta, String)} methods.
3500       *
3501       * <h4 class='section'>Example:</h4>
3502       * <p class='bjava'>
3503       *    <jc>// Define a POJO swap that skips serializing beans if the time zone is GMT.</jc>
3504       *    <jk>public class</jk> MyBeanSwap <jk>extends</jk> StringSwap&lt;MyBean&gt; {
3505       *       <ja>@Override</ja>
3506       *       <jk>public</jk> String swap(MarshallingSession <jv>session</jv>, MyBean <jv>bean</jv>) <jk>throws</jk> Exception {
3507       *          <jk>if</jk> (<jv>session</jv>.getTimeZone().equals(TimeZone.<jsf>GMT</jsf>))
3508       *             <jk>return null</jk>;
3509       *          <jk>return</jk> <jv>bean</jv>.toString();
3510       *       }
3511       *    }
3512       *
3513       *    <jc>// Create a serializer that uses GMT if the timezone is not specified in the session args.</jc>
3514       *    WriterSerializer <jv>serializer</jv> = JsonSerializer
3515       *       .<jsm>create</jsm>()
3516       *       .timeZone(TimeZone.<jsf>GMT</jsf>)
3517       *       .build();
3518       * </p>
3519       *
3520       * <h4 class='section'>See Also:</h4><ul>
3521       *    <li class='ja'>{@link MarshalledConfig#timeZone()}
3522       *    <li class='jm'>{@link MarshallingSession.Builder#timeZone(TimeZone)}
3523       * </ul>
3524       *
3525       * @param value The new value for this property.
3526       *    <br>Can be <jk>null</jk> (timezone will not be set, defaults to system timezone).
3527       * @return This object.
3528       */
3529      public Builder timeZone(TimeZone value) {
3530         timeZone = value;
3531         return this;
3532      }

4065   /**
4066    * Checks if the specified class should be cached.
4067    *
4068    * <p>
4069    * Generated classes (proxies, lambda expressions, etc.) shouldn't be cacheable to prevent
4070    * needlessly filling up the cache.
4071    *
4072    * @param c The class to check.
4073    * @return <jk>true</jk> if the class should be cached.
4074    */
4075   private static boolean isCacheable(Class<?> c) {
4076      var n = c.getName();
4077      var x = n.charAt(n.length() - 1);  // All generated classes appear to end with digits.
4078      return !((x >= '0' && x <= '9') && (n.indexOf("$$") != -1 || n.startsWith("sun") || n.startsWith("com.sun") || n.indexOf("$Proxy") != -1));
4079   }

4277         .beanTypePropertyName(typePropertyName)
4278         .notBeanPackageNames(notBeanPackageNames)
4279         .notBeanPackagePrefixes(notBeanPackagePrefixes)
4280         .notBeanClasses(notBeanClasses.stream().map(ClassInfo::inner).toList())
4281         .beanStore(beanStore)
4282         .annotationProvider(getAnnotationProvider())
4283         .beanMetaInitializer(MarshalledBeanMetaInitializer.INSTANCE)
4284         .beanPropertyPostProcessor(MarshalledPropertyPostProcessor.INSTANCE)
4285         .build();
4286   }

4398   /**
4399    * Fallback for an ObjectSwap-conversion whose swap-class doesn't bridge to the input, but where the input
4400    * is already a {@link Map} matching the target's own Map shape -- copies its entries into a new instance
4401    * of the target type rather than dropping the value as {@code null}.
4402    *
4403    * @param toMeta The target type.
4404    * @param in The input value.
4405    * @return A new map instance of the target type populated with the input's entries, or <jk>null</jk> if
4406    *    the target isn't Map-shaped or the input isn't a {@link Map}.
4407    */
4408   private static Object copyMapEntries(ClassMeta<?> toMeta, Object in) {
4409      if (! (toMeta.isMap() && in instanceof Map<?,?> in2))
4410         return null;
4411      var result = (Map<Object,Object>) (toMeta.canCreateNewInstance() ? toMeta.newInstance() : new LinkedHashMap<>());
4412      result.putAll(in2);
4413      return result;
4414   }
